history.period: 14th century CE (one source claims 10th-11th c. Rashtrakuta-early Western Chalukya - flagged below)
history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: This temple is already recorded = seq 995 (id dichpally-ramalayam-nizamabad, name "Sri Rama Temple"); keep-or-drop/merge decision needed for a duplicates pair. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Nizamabad' is the district; the temple is at Dichpally village, ~19 km from Nizamabad city. Identity confirmed: the famous Khilla (fort) Ramalayam of Dichpally, one of Nizamabad district's best-known ancient temples, built in white and black basalt stone. 'Khilla' (fort) refers to the fort that once surrounded the temple (alternate account: the fort name was adopted as a protective ruse against invading armies); the sanctum's vimana is missing and the temple was left incomplete (one account dates abandonment to 1311 AD). It is celebrated for Kakatiya-style stone carvings - four-petal flower motifs, goddesses, animals, pillars and artistic beams, with erotic/Kamasutra-style panels on the upper outer walls - earning it the nickname 'Khajuraho of Telangana'. The present murtis of Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman were installed in 1949, gifted by local devotee Gajawada Chinnaiah. DATE FLAG: trawell and telangana360 place it in the Kakatiya 14th century; templesnow claims 10th-11th c. Rashtrakuta-early Western Chalukya origins - treat the earlier date as unverified. Recognised as a protected heritage site; a lake lies to the temple's south and the temple becomes a virtual island during monsoon.

name: Dichpally Ramalayam
town_description: Dichpally is a village/mandal in Nizamabad district, Telangana, on NH-44. The temple stands on a small hillock in the middle of the village, reached by ~100-105 steps, with a lake on its southern side.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~160-210 km; sources vary).
travel.railway: Dichpally railway station (~4 km); Nizamabad railway station (~19 km).
travel.road: Near NH-44; about 19 km from Nizamabad bus station and 4 km from Dichpally bus stand; cab or auto.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (pleasant); monsoon visits show the temple as an island but access can be difficult. Sri Rama Navami is the grandest festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-8:00 PM daily. Entry free; ~105 steps to climb (not wheelchair-friendly).
